concepts.title: Sources of Error: Truncation, Rounding, Propagation
concepts.summary: Where numerical error comes from: truncating an infinite process, rounding to finite precision, and how both propagate through a computation, with absolute and relative error and loss of significance.

concepts.title: Conditioning and Numerical Stability
concepts.summary: The conditioning of a problem versus the stability of an algorithm, forward and backward error, and why a well-conditioned problem can still be ruined by an unstable formula.

concepts.title: Bisection and Convergence Rate

related.label: Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem

concepts.summary: Bisection as a numerical method: the bracketing guarantee from the Intermediate Value Theorem, linear convergence, the exact iteration count for a tolerance, and stopping criteria.

concepts.title: Fixed-Point Iteration
concepts.summary: Fixed-point iteration, the contraction condition on the derivative that decides convergence, and how rewriting the same equation changes the outcome.

concepts.title: Newton's Method

related.label: Taylor and Maclaurin Series with Error Bounds

concepts.summary: Newton's method derived from the tangent line, quadratic convergence near a simple root, and how it fails: poor starting points, vanishing derivatives, and multiple roots.

concepts.title: Secant Method and Order of Convergence
concepts.summary: The secant method as Newton without a derivative, the formal definition of order of convergence, and how the secant method's order is derived.

concepts.title: LU Decomposition and Partial Pivoting

related.label: Gaussian Elimination and Row Echelon Form
The Simplex Method: Tableau and Pivoting

concepts.summary: LU decomposition as Gaussian elimination with its multipliers recorded, why partial pivoting is required for stability, PA = LU, and reusing the factors across right-hand sides. This pivoting is not the simplex pivot, and the lesson says so.

concepts.title: Iterative Methods: Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel
concepts.summary: Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iterations for large sparse systems, the diagonal dominance and spectral radius conditions for convergence, and when iteration beats factorization.

concepts.title: The Matrix Condition Number
concepts.summary: The condition number of a matrix, how it bounds the amplification of relative error in Ax = b, and the Hilbert matrix as the classic ill-conditioned case.

concepts.title: Polynomial Interpolation: Lagrange and Newton
concepts.summary: The Lagrange and Newton forms of the same interpolating polynomial, divided differences, the interpolation error formula, and Runge's phenomenon.

concepts.title: Splines
concepts.summary: Piecewise interpolation with linear and cubic splines, the continuity conditions, natural and clamped boundaries, and why splines avoid Runge's oscillation.

concepts.title: Least-Squares Curve Fitting
concepts.summary: Fitting curves by least squares from the numerical side: normal equations versus QR, conditioning, and the choice of basis, building on the linear algebra lesson instead of repeating it.

concepts.title: Trapezoid and Simpson Rules

related.label: The Definite Integral and Riemann Sums

concepts.summary: The composite trapezoid and Simpson rules derived from interpolation, with their error terms worked on integrals that have known exact values.

concepts.title: Error Orders and Adaptive Quadrature
concepts.summary: The order of a quadrature rule, Richardson extrapolation, and adaptive quadrature that refines only where the error estimate demands it.

concepts.title: Euler's Method and Local vs Global Error
concepts.summary: Euler's method for initial-value problems, local truncation error versus global error, the effect of step size, and a first look at stability.

concepts.title: Runge-Kutta Methods
concepts.summary: Second-order and classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta methods, how they gain order without derivatives of the right-hand side, and adaptive step size.

concepts.title: Choosing a Numerical Method: A Decision Guide
concepts.summary: A decision guide for the whole discipline: given a problem's size, smoothness, and conditioning, choose a method and diagnose why it failed.
